items.quote: The microstructure observations and quantitative measurements were performed using a FE-SEM (TESCAN MIRA 3) equipped with EDX.
The XRD patterns were collected by an X-ray diffractometer (PANayltical Empyrean, Cu-Kα) at 40 kV and 40 mA from 20 to 90◦ in a scan step 5◦ /min.

The proper amounts of pure metals Co (99.99 wt.%), Cu (99.99 wt. %) and Zr (99.95 wt.%) about 4 g were weighed, and then melted in argon atmosphere using an arc-furnace (SKY DHL-400) with nonconsumable tungsten electrode. During the arc-melting, every ingot was turned over at least five times to ensure homogeneity.

Subsequently, these ingots were enclosed in evacuated quartz capsules and annealed at 1023 K for 60 days in a chamber-furnace (MTI KSL-1200). After that, they were quenched in water and cut into two pieces (Struers Secotom15).
One was mounted and polished for microstructure study, and the other was crushed in a steel mortar, grinded up in an agate mortar and annealed at 873 K for 2 h for XRD analysis.
